source.original_question:
Lines l, m, and n are perpendicular bisectors of \triangle P Q R. If T Q = 2 x, P T = 3 y - 1, and T R = 8, find z.
Choices:
A:3
B:4
C:5
D:6

audit.source_question:
Lines l, m, and n are perpendicular bisectors of \triangle P Q R. If T Q = 2 x, P T = 3 y - 1, and T R = 8, find z.

adaptation.reason: Original double-arrow length cues are represented by perpendicular-endpoint protocol distance markers; the three perpendicular-bisector lines are frozen display clips. No extra right-angle marks are added.

audit.independent_solution: Line l bisects PR, so PO=OR. The labeled halves give z+4=7, hence z=3, option A. The other labels are consistent with the common circumradius 8: x=4 and y=3.
audit.geometry_notes: Coordinates were analytically constructed from the stated conditions. Computed lengths freeze a faithful shape without exposing the answer as a label. Source connections, point order, mathematical labels and relation groups were compared visually; any necessary condition or representation changes are described in adaptation.reason. Display-only coordinates do not add question conditions.

source_visual_review.method: Viewed original image at readable scale before native geometric construction

redraw_visual_review.note: Compared P/Q/R/T, all three bisectors and radius labels. Moved 2x to clear both adjacent lines; retained z+4 and 7 as two distinct base-half distance markers. Source line arrowheads are represented as frozen display clips.
